work_packages.title: Create the Cargo workspace and the architecture checks
work_packages.summary: Create the workspace with the twelve library crates and four binaries from ADR 0002 as empty compiling shells. A shell has no dependencies and only a short crate comment; the package that owns the crate adds its dependencies and its module declarations. Each crate inherits the workspace lints, and the four crates that must stay free of I/O carry their clippy ban list. Every binary prints that it is not implemented and exits with an error. External dependency versions are pinned in the manifest of the crate that uses them, so parallel packages never edit the root manifest. Write the xtask architecture check test-first, including the source-scan rules that the negative-test catalog lists as static checks. This package merges before any other package touches a crate directory.

done.check: The workspace builds from a clean checkout.
The architecture check passes on the skeleton.
Each rule DEP-01 to DEP-04 and DEP-08 to DEP-10 has a failing fixture that makes the check exit non-zero.

Static checks ST-01 (no safe.directory wildcard), ST-02 (no equality comparison on signatures), ST-03 (no shell spawn), ST-04 (dangerous container flags only in the posture verifier deny list and tests), ST-05 (no merge or deploy path without the approval check) and ST-09 (workspace reads only through the ingestion module) each have a failing fixture.
The clippy bans fire: a scratch crate using each banned call fails under the same clippy.toml.
Lints and formatting are clean.
The set of crates in cargo metadata equals the set in crate-dependency-rules.json, so every listed crate and binary exists as an empty compiling shell.
Every crate sets [lints] workspace = true, and a crate that does not fails the architecture check (DEP-06).

work_packages.title: Implement the PostgreSQL store, the evidence ledger and the local artifact store
work_packages.summary: Implement Store and Tx over Diesel with diesel-async, claim and lease operations, outbox writes, the ledger with chain verification, and LocalFsArtifactStore. The shared contract suite from testkit runs against it. Follow the notes in docs/database/for-the-storage-crate.md and ADR 0012. Claims lock with FOR NO KEY UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Store::begin makes the tenant setting as its first statement, the system scope uses its own role and pool, and the two lookups outside a transaction use the narrow functions. The isolation tests run as the application login. No database message or detail text ever reaches an API client. Built to the ports-v1.1 shape (ADR 0014): SystemTx for the candidate search and the due-attempt queries, start_attempt as the DBA's two-step claim with the lease on the attempt, inserts that are idempotent by id and content, the listings, Store::committed to settle an unknown commit outcome, record_platform_audit under the platform tenant, resolve_installation with the repository id, and an artifact store whose get and exists join the tenant's index row.

done.check: The store contract suite passes against PgStore on PostgreSQL in Docker, the same suite that passes against the in-memory fake.
Two workers that find the same candidate: exactly one start_attempt wins, the loser gets Conflict, and the winner's stage run is RUNNING at epoch plus one with its attempt in STARTING.
A zombie worker's write with an old lease epoch is rejected.
A fault injected after the outbox insert rolls back the status change, the ledger entry and the outbox row together.
Every repository method refuses to return or change another tenant's rows.

Concurrent appends to one job give a continuous, verifiable chain. The test that flips one byte of a stored entry does it as the table owner with the ledger trigger disabled (ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER), and the verifier then fails.
The first append test reproduces the two published hash vectors of docs/database/ledger-and-audit.md, so the database check and the domain function agree.
The artifact store is idempotent, verifies hashes on read, detects a corrupted blob and writes read-only files.

The application role cannot UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or DROP the audit tables (NT-AUD-01), and the audit events carry actor, policy hash and correlation id.
Claims use FOR NO KEY UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, shown by a ledger append that is not blocked while a claimer holds the stage run.

Every tenant transaction makes the tenant setting first. Run as the application login with two tenants, a call for tenant A never reads or changes tenant B's rows and a call with no tenant sees nothing (NT-TEN-01, Rust part). The store refuses to become ready when its role can bypass row-level security or owns the tables.

done.check: The two lookups outside a transaction answer None for every miss reason, so a caller cannot tell an unknown token from an expired one, and resolve_installation needs the pair of installation and repository ids.
Every database error maps to the closed StoreError. The message and detail text of the database, which can name another tenant's key value, never reach a caller and are logged only after redaction.

A connection that drops after COMMIT was sent is reported as an unknown outcome, and Store::committed answers from the witness whether the transaction was applied, shown with a fault injected between the commit and the reply.

work_packages.title: Implement the GitHub App adapter for issues, narrowed tokens, draft pull requests and webhooks
work_packages.summary: Implement IssueSource and ChangeHost as a GitHub App: sign the App JWT, mint one installation token per job narrowed to one repository and to the permissions of one stage, revoke it at job end, verify webhook signatures on the raw body, deduplicate deliveries, run the repository protection preflight, push only to factory branches, and write only sanitized text. Merging is not implemented. Requester authorization is the named allowlist from policy, not a GitHub role.
